All other coverage (AC1-AC5, AC7-AC11, actor_id-nil dispositions) was already validated PASS in that same report and is unchanged in this pass.

(1) THE ORDER-SENSITIVITY GAP. Re-derived the reasoning from scratch against the real code (lib/letflow/audit.ex lines 273-302) before writing anything: prev_chain_hash IS one of the 11 canonical-form fields hashed into chain_hash (field 11, fields_from_entry/1 includes it, canonical_string/1 hashes fields.prev_chain_hash). So a raw-SQL tamper of ONLY a persisted entry's prev_chain_hash column (leaving that entry's own chain_hash column untouched) makes BOTH of do_verify_chain/2's cond clauses true simultaneously for that same entry: the recompute check fails (fields_from_entry/1 now reads the tampered prev_chain_hash, so the freshly recomputed hash no longer matches the untouched stored chain_hash), AND the linkage check fails (the tampered prev_chain_hash no longer equals the previous entry's own recomputed hash). Since Elixir's cond returns its first true branch, which of {:error, {:hash_mismatch, id}} / {:error, {:chain_broken, id}} comes back is decided ENTIRELY by check order -- this is genuinely order-sensitive, not vacuous; the two orderings are behaviorally distinguishable for exactly this construction (contrary to the alternative hypothesis the rework prompt asked me to rule out first). No 'internally-self-consistent-but-non-linked' construction was needed -- the direct single-column tamper the design doc and audit_test.exs's own code comment (lines 244-252) already name by example is itself the distinguishing case; audit_test.exs's existing chain_broken test (deleted middle row) and hash_mismatch test (after_state-only tamper) each leave the other check's condition false, which is precisely why neither one exercises this order dependency.

Added one new test, test/letflow/audit_dispositions_test.exs describe block 'AC6 -- check order: a prev_chain_hash-only tamper is hash_mismatch, not chain_broken': inserts two chained entries, disables the immutability trigger, overwrites entry 2's prev_chain_hash column (only) with a valid-shaped-but-wrong SHA-256 hex string via raw SQL, re-enables the trigger, and asserts Audit.verify_chain/2 returns {:error, {:hash_mismatch, id_2}} (not chain_broken) against the real, shipped, reverted implementation.

  - Mutation reverted via `git checkout -- lib/letflow/audit.ex`; `git status --porcelain lib/` empty afterward; full target suite re-confirmed green (25 passed) with the reverted implementation.
